text: Finally the king put down the spade. <break time="0.8s" /> And said. <break time="0.8s" /> I came to you for answers, wise man. <break time="0.8s" /> If you cannot give me any. <break time="0.8s" /> Tell me so. <break time="0.8s" /> And I will go home. <break time="0.8s" /> Someone is running toward us. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the hermit. <break time="0.8s" /> Let us see who it is. <break time="0.8s" /> The king turned and saw. <break time="0.8s" /> A bearded man running out of the woods. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> Against his stomach. <break time="0.8s" /> Blood was flowing. <break time="0.8s" /> From under his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> And when he reached the king. <break time="0.8s" /> He fell to the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> The king and the hermit. <break time="0.8s" /> Opened his clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> And found a deep wound. <break time="0.8s" /> In his stomach. <break time="0.8s" /> The king washed the wound. <break time="0.8s" /> And covered it. <break time="0.8s" /> With his handkerchief. <break time="0.8s" /> And a towel that the hermit had. <break time="0.8s" /> The blood soaked through again and again. <break time="0.8s" /> But the king kept changing the bandage. <break time="0.8s" /> Until it stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> When the man felt a little better. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked for a drink. <break time="0.8s" /> So the king brought him. <break time="0.8s" /> Fresh water. <break time="0.8s" /> By then the sun had set. <break time="0.8s" /> And the air had become cool. <break time="0.8s" /> So they carried the man. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the hut. <break time="0.8s" /> The king was so tired. <break time="0.8s" /> That he lay down on the doorstep. <break time="0.8s" /> And slept through the short summer night.
